descriptionChirho: The heavens or sky as the visible expanse above the earth, including the atmosphere where birds fly, clouds form, and rain falls, as well as the cosmic vault where celestial bodies are set; the most common absolute and articulated forms of shamayim in all grammatical positions.

The heavens as a locative domain — the place where something exists or occurs, often expressing God's dwelling place or the cosmic sphere where divine action takes place; includes prepositional beth ('in') and related locative constructions.
The heavens as a source or origin — the place from which God speaks, sends rain, fire, or manna, or from which divine action proceeds downward to earth; marked by preposition min ('from').

The heavens as a goal or direction — the place toward which one looks, lifts hands, or ascends; includes directional he, preposition lamed ('to'), and the -ward suffix indicating motion or orientation heavenward.
The heavens in construct state, bound to a following genitive — 'heavens of heavens,' 'heavens of the LORD,' expressing the superlative cosmic realm or possessive relationship with deity or creation.

The heavens with pronominal suffixes indicating personal possession or association — 'your heavens,' 'his heavens' — expressing the heavens as belonging to or associated with God or a human addressee, often in poetic or liturgical contexts.
